product.name: JobFinder
product.summary: A web app that learns who you are (questionnaire + resume/portfolio/GitHub/socials), scrapes and caches job postings, matches and ranks them against your profile, drafts cover letters, emails a daily digest of new matches, and emails targeted questions when it is unsure about a job. Primarily for software/engineering roles, usable for any industry.
product.target_users: A small, select group of people (multi-user, low volume). Not a high-scale public service. Access is by invitation only: the owner adds accounts manually (see REQ-18 / DESIGN-01).

stack.frontend: Vite + React + TypeScript, TanStack Query, react-router
stack.ai: Claude Code CLI (headless claude -p) on the owner's Claude subscription; no SDK, no API key
stack.email: Self-hosted SMTP in docker (boky/postfix); Mailpit in dev
stack.deploy: docker compose: db, api, worker, web (Caddy, TLS), smtp, mailpit (dev profile)
stack.storage: Docker volume file store (backend/jobfinder/storage) for uploads and fetched link text

requirements.requirement: Ask about job-search status: new grad or not and when, when a job is needed by, where the person expects to live (locations, remote preference, relocation), salary expectations (min/target), how prestigious the job should be, company size, industries, target roles and seniority, visa sponsorship.
requirements.notes: Stored as profiles.status JSONB; profile version bumps on every change so match scores can be cached per version.

requirements.requirement: Ask about background: internships/co-ops/previous jobs and what was done in each, projects, skills, education. Extract this from uploaded material, then let the user review and edit it.
requirements.notes: Verified with a real model call: no invented facts, and an injected 'ignore previous instructions' line in a resume was ignored. The extracted background now also has a `name` (used to sign cover letters), editable in the review step.

requirements.requirement: Ask adaptive follow-up questions about what the person does and why they do it well ("have you done X?"); answers become stored facts used in matching and cover letters.
requirements.notes: Answers are saved as profile_facts via POST /api/profile/facts.

requirements.requirement: Accept resume and portfolio files (PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD up to 10MB), and links to GitHub, portfolio sites and socials. Files and link snapshots are kept in a docker-volume file store (not Postgres) with an ID and tags for easy retrieval.
requirements.notes: Store layout /data/store/{user_id}/{doc_id}/{meta.json,original.<ext>,text.txt}; doc_id is doc_ + ms-timestamp hex + random hex (sorts by creation time). Automatic tags (kind, ext, source, url, link_kind) plus user tags; list filter by kind and tag=key:value; GET /api/documents/{id}, /download, /text; PUT /tags; duplicate uploads (same sha256) return the existing document. Atomic writes. GitHub summarised via the public API; portfolio/other pages fetched with an SSRF guard; LinkedIn and X stored but not fetched. DocumentStore is an interface so S3/MinIO can replace it later.

requirements.requirement: Multi-user accounts, kept simple: a users table and a sessions table in Postgres, httpOnly session cookie.
requirements.notes: argon2 password hashes. No email verification or password reset (intentionally out of scope for now). Admin role: users.is_admin; the first account created is admin and ADMIN_EMAILS can grant more (also applied at login). Signup records the browser's timezone for the daily email. PLANNED CHANGE: self-signup and the first-user-admin rule are superseded by REQ-18 (invite-only accounts activated by an emailed set-password link); admin will come only from ADMIN_EMAILS.

requirements.requirement: Dockerized stack: FastAPI + uv backend, Postgres database, Vite + TypeScript frontend.
requirements.notes: Host ports: web 8180, api 8100, db 5433 (all localhost-only).

requirements.requirement: Use Claude Code so the user's Claude subscription powers all AI features (no API key). AI layer is written specifically for this project.
requirements.notes: Runs only in the worker. No tools, restricted mode, prompt over stdin, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY scrubbed from the child env, schema-validated output with one repair retry, error classification (auth/rate_limited/timeout/bad_output/cli_missing), concurrency cap, per-call logging to ai_calls. Remaining AI functions (score_match, already_answered, cover_letter) are not written yet. Connecting Claude is done from the web app (REQ-16). Auth failures from the CLI ('Not logged in', '401 ... OAuth access token is invalid') are classified as auth.

requirements.requirement: Use an SMTP service run through docker for email (low volume, small group).
requirements.notes: send_email() over aiosmtplib (multipart text+HTML, long headers kept as plain URLs). Dev: Mailpit (docker --profile dev, SMTP 1025, UI 8025). Production: the internal `smtp` postfix service relaying through Gmail with the owner's app password (kept only in the git-ignored root .env). Verified: a real test message went app -> postfix -> Gmail and Gmail accepted it (250 2.0.0 OK); the owner still needs to confirm it landed in the inbox rather than spam. `python -m jobfinder.cli test-email --to you@example.com` sends a test.

requirements.requirement: Scrape/collect job postings, covering ATS boards (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby) and LinkedIn/Indeed, and cache them in Postgres.
requirements.notes: 27 verified company boards (19 Greenhouse, 2 Lever, 6 Ashby) seeded from companies.yaml; ~7,100 active jobs cached in Postgres (jobs, companies tables). Each posting is normalised to a common shape (clean-text description, workplace type, seniority, salary from structured fields or parsed from the text, dedupe hash). Upsert is idempotent (ON CONFLICT); jobs missing from a successful fetch are deactivated, with a guard so an empty response from a large board is treated as a glitch; per-company error isolation, one retry on 5xx/timeout. LinkedIn/Indeed via python-jobspy is opt-in (ENABLE_JOBSPY, `uv sync --extra jobspy`, WITH_JOBSPY build arg), queries built from users' target roles x locations, jobs expire after 14 days unseen. Run with `python -m jobfinder.cli ingest [--ats X] [--company slug] [--jobspy]`; also registered as the `ingest_jobs` worker task. Not scheduled yet (milestone 7). Ingestion now also runs on a schedule (see REQ-17).

requirements.requirement: Match each user with jobs: hard filters, cheap prefilter, then LLM scoring (score, confidence, verdict, reasons, unknowns), cached per profile version, budgeted per user per day.
requirements.notes: Pipeline per user: hard filters (active, level, location/remote preference, salary floor when pay is known, visa-sponsorship refusals when sponsorship is needed, 'N+ years of experience' for entry-level candidates) -> prefilter score 0-100 (title similarity 45, skill overlap 35, recency 10, prestige fit 10, +/- size and industry) -> top candidates go to Claude (haiku) for a score 0-100, confidence 0-1, reasons, gaps and unknowns; verdict (strong/good/stretch/no) is derived from the score in code. Unknown data never excludes a job. Budget: MATCH_DAILY_LLM_BUDGET (default 25) LLM-scored jobs per user per rolling 24h, best prefilter first; progress is committed per job so a rate limit loses nothing and the task retries. One row per distinct posting (dedupe_hash). Profile changes: saved matches and promising new ones are re-scored (saved first), dismissed/applied are not; user status is kept. Triggers: onboarding finish, the 'Find new matches' button, and after the ingest_jobs task. Feed: tabs (To review/Saved/Applied/Dismissed with counts), filters (min score, workplace, search, sort), score badge, reasons and gaps, Save/Mark applied/Dismiss, job detail page with description and the questions that would sharpen the score; closed jobs are hidden unless saved or applied. Verified live with the real model: 701 -> 400 candidates after adding the experience filter, 7 of 10 scored jobs were good/stretch fits for a new-grad backend profile.

requirements.requirement: Draft a cover letter for a job from the user's profile and facts, never inventing experience; editable, regenerable, downloadable.
requirements.notes: Drafted on demand from a match (job detail page) by Claude (sonnet) in the worker, from the candidate's real background, the answers they gave, the job posting and the match analysis (strengths/gaps). Four tones (professional, warm, concise, enthusiastic) and an optional 'anything to emphasize' note. Prompt guardrails: use only facts in the profile, never invent employers/metrics/skills/feelings, never state that the candidate lacks something, no salary or visa talk, no placeholders; untrusted posting text is delimited as data; output with [placeholders] or too short is retried once then rejected. One current letter per user+job in Postgres (cover_letters); editable in the app (marks it 'edited'), redraft needs confirmation (API requires force) when edited, delete, copy, download as a plain Word .docx; a letter drafted before a profile update is flagged. The page resumes watching a draft after a reload. The sign-off uses a new `name` field extracted from the resume and editable in the background review step. Verified with the real model: facts, metrics, dates and employers match the profile; after tightening the prompt the letter no longer asserts missing skills or invented enjoyment.

requirements.requirement: Daily digest email of new matching job openings, sent at the user's local digest hour.
requirements.notes: One daily email per user at their chosen local hour (timezone captured at signup, editable in Settings), sent by an hourly worker task: due from the chosen hour for 6 hours, once per local day, never an empty email. Contents: up to 10 new good matches (score 65+, status new, not yet emailed, job still open) with score, reasons, View and Apply links, plus the clarifying questions section; matches/questions are marked sent only after the SMTP server accepts the message. Separate opt-outs (digest, question emails); one-click unsubscribe link and List-Unsubscribe headers; Settings page with hour/timezone/toggles and a 'send me a preview' button (marks nothing as sent). HTML output is escaped (job text is untrusted).

requirements.requirement: When unsure about a job (could be good but low confidence), email the user questions about the opening ("have you done X?"); answers feed back into the profile and the job is rescored.
requirements.notes: Matches with confidence below 0.6 but score 50+ (could be good, we're unsure) have their `unknowns` collected; a haiku call merges duplicates and paraphrases across jobs, drops anything the profile facts already answer or that was asked/skipped before, and caps the list (max 8 open, 6 per email). Questions go out in the daily email with a signed 14-day link that works without logging in (separate salts per purpose, tamper/expiry checked), and also appear in the in-app Questions inbox with a nav badge. Answers become profile facts (source job_question), bump the profile version and queue a matching run so affected matches are re-scored; users can skip. Verified with the real model: 5 raw questions became 2 (three AI-tool variants merged, the already-answered one dropped), the email link answered/skipped questions from a logged-out browser, and the matches were re-scored afterwards.

requirements.requirement: Pages for matches feed, job detail with cover letter, questions inbox, profile editing and settings (digest time/enabled).
requirements.notes: All planned pages exist: login/signup (with redirect back after login), onboarding wizard, matches feed, job detail with cover letter, Questions inbox, no-login question link page, Profile (edit preferences, background, resume & links, delete answers), Settings (email schedule, timezone, preview) and AI setup (admin). Header navigation with a questions badge.

requirements.requirement: Documents and similar blobs (uploads, fetched link text) are kept in a bucket/docker volume rather than Postgres tables, each with an ID and tags so they are easy to retrieve.
requirements.notes: Docker volume `store` mounted at /data/store in api and worker. Layout: /data/store/{user_id}/{doc_id}/{meta.json, original.<ext>, text.txt}. doc_id = 'doc_' + millisecond-timestamp hex + random hex, so IDs sort by creation time. Automatic tags (kind, ext, source, url, link_kind) plus user-defined tags; list filter ?kind= and ?tag=key:value (repeatable); GET /api/documents/{id}, /download, /text; PUT /tags; identical uploads deduplicated by sha256; writes are atomic (temp dir then rename); IDs validated so paths cannot escape the user directory. DocumentStore is an interface: an S3/MinIO implementation can replace it without touching callers. Postgres keeps only structured relational data; cover letters (milestone 6) stay in Postgres. Retrieval examples: GET /api/documents?tag=target:backend, GET /api/documents/{id}/download.

requirements.requirement: Claude Code can be connected from outside the worker container: an admin pastes the long-lived token from `claude setup-token` into an in-app page, tests it, and can disconnect it, with no .env editing, container shell or restart.
requirements.notes: Token stored as a 0600 file on the `claude-auth` docker volume (/data/claude/oauth_token) shared by api (writes) and worker (reads before every call, so changes apply immediately). Precedence: saved token, then CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN env, then the CLI's own login. Endpoints: GET /api/ai/status (any user; never returns the token), PUT/DELETE /api/admin/ai/token and POST /api/admin/ai/check (admin only); the check runs an `ai_check` task in the worker and reports the real error. Frontend: admin-only /settings/ai page (status, steps, paste token, Test connection, Disconnect), an 'AI isn't connected' banner on the wizard's resume step, and failure notices that send admins to the setup page and tell other users to ask the admin. Verified in a browser against the docker stack: the worker used the pasted token (the CLI reached Anthropic and got a 401 for a fake one) and the page showed the real error. Still to confirm with a real token: a successful call from the docker worker.

requirements.requirement: Ingestion, matching and emails run automatically without anyone pressing a button.
requirements.notes: APScheduler in the worker enqueues `ingest_jobs` every INGEST_INTERVAL_HOURS (default 6; first run 2 minutes after start) and `daily_emails` hourly at :05, through the same Postgres queue as everything else (deduped so runs never pile up). After ingestion a matching run is queued for every user who finished onboarding; after matching, question collection is queued. Queue dedupe now distinguishes tasks by payload. SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false turns it off. Verified live: the scheduler enqueued and ran an ingest of all 27 boards, which queued matching and question collection.

requirements.requirement: Access is by invitation only: there is no self-signup. The owner adds accounts manually as email-only rows (everything else NULL). On the sign-in page, anyone whose email is in the table but has no password set, or who forgot theirs, can request an emailed link to set a password; setting it activates the account and populates the row.
acceptance: POST /api/auth/signup and the sign-up UI no longer exist
Signing in with an unknown email, a pending (no password yet) account or a wrong password gives the same generic error, with equal work done so timing does not reveal which
Requesting a link for an unknown email sends nothing and returns exactly the same response as for a known email
A set-password link works once, expires after 60 minutes, and is invalidated by the password change itself
Setting the password signs the user in, ends all of their other sessions, and fills in their timezone, email settings and an empty profile
Pending (never-activated) rows receive no emails, no matching and no scheduler work
Admin status comes only from ADMIN_EMAILS; the 'first account created is admin' rule is removed
Link requests and failed logins are rate limited per email and per real client IP

decisions.decision: Multi-user with simple users + sessions tables; no auth library, OAuth or email verification.
decisions.reason: User asked to keep auth shallow for now.

decisions.decision: Public ATS APIs (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby) plus opt-in LinkedIn/Indeed via python-jobspy.
decisions.reason: ATS APIs are stable and structured; user also wants LinkedIn/Indeed coverage, so it is isolated behind a flag and allowed to fail.

decisions.decision: Own AI layer on the Claude Code CLI using the user's subscription; nothing ported from the samai project; no Anthropic SDK or API key.
decisions.reason: User's explicit instruction. Usage limits are therefore shared by all users, so calls are budgeted and concurrency-capped.

decisions.decision: Self-hosted SMTP in docker (boky/postfix), relay mode through Gmail/Outlook by default, direct mode optional; Mailpit in dev. Users answer questions via signed in-app links.
decisions.reason: User asked for SMTP via docker for a small group; relay mode gets inbox delivery without DNS/port-25 setup.

decisions.decision: AI runs only in the worker container; the API enqueues Postgres tasks and the UI polls GET /api/tasks/{id}.
decisions.reason: Keeps the claude CLI out of the request path and the api image; gives retries and backoff for rate limits.

decisions.decision: API 8100, web 8180, db 5433, all bound to 127.0.0.1.
decisions.reason: Port 8000 is used by another local project; db port lets host-side pytest and alembic reach Postgres.

decisions.decision: Documents and fetched-link text live in a docker volume file store with generated IDs and tags (meta.json per document); Postgres keeps only structured relational data. Cover letters (milestone 6) stay in Postgres.
decisions.reason: User asked for a bucket/volume instead of Postgres tables; a plain volume is the simplest option for a small group and the DocumentStore interface allows moving to S3/MinIO later.

decisions.decision: Jobs are keyed by (source, external_id) and cross-source duplicates are found via dedupe_hash (company+title+location, normalised) rather than merged at write time; a job missing from a successful board fetch is marked inactive, never deleted.
decisions.reason: Keeps ingestion simple and idempotent; matching (milestone 5) can pick one row per dedupe_hash. Inactive rows preserve history for matches already shown.

decisions.decision: One shared subscription token, set by an admin on an in-app page and stored as a 0600 file on a dedicated credentials docker volume that the worker re-reads on every call. The first account created is admin (ADMIN_EMAILS can add more); once DEC-14 is built, admin comes only from ADMIN_EMAILS. The env var stays as a fallback.
decisions.reason: The token flow is the supported headless path; driving an interactive browser login inside the container would mean parsing a terminal session. A volume file keeps the secret out of Postgres, the file store and the repo, and avoids restarts.

decisions.decision: Deterministic hard filters and a cheap prefilter rank the cached jobs first; only the top few per user per day reach the LLM (haiku, one job per call, strict JSON schema). The verdict is computed from the score in code, not trusted from the model. Unknown job data never excludes a job. Entry-level candidates are not shown roles asking for 3+ years of experience.
decisions.reason: Your Claude subscription limits and ~25s per scored job make blind LLM scoring of ~7,000 jobs impossible; live testing showed 7 of 10 early calls were wasted on obviously over-level roles before the experience filter was added.

decisions.decision: Letters are generated asynchronously in the worker per match, stored as one editable current draft per user+job in Postgres (not the file store), and the API refuses to overwrite a user-edited draft unless forced. The queue's dedupe now distinguishes tasks by payload so different matches/options are separate tasks.
decisions.reason: Generation takes seconds to a minute and must survive page reloads; letters are small, relational (tied to a job) and user-edited, so Postgres fits; protecting user edits avoids silent data loss.

decisions.decision: New matches and clarifying questions share one daily email per user at their chosen local hour (with separate opt-outs and a one-click unsubscribe), rather than separate emails per job or per question. Question links use signed tokens so they work without logging in; every other link (view/apply) goes through the normal login.
decisions.reason: Avoids spamming a small group of users; answering a question should take seconds from a phone, so it can't require a login; the signed, expiring, purpose-scoped token keeps that safe.

decisions.decision: One LLM call per collection run merges paraphrased questions across jobs and drops those already answered or previously asked, instead of one 'already answered?' call per question.
decisions.reason: Cheaper on the shared subscription and sees all questions at once, so it can merge duplicates across jobs, which per-question checks cannot.

decisions.decision: Invite-only accounts with an emailed set/reset-password link. There is no self-signup: the owner adds each account manually as a row containing only an email (all other columns NULL). Signing in with a known email that has no password yet, or a forgotten one, offers 'email me a link'; the link lets the person choose a password, which activates the account and populates the row. Unknown emails get nothing. Supersedes the open signup and the first-user-admin rule (admin only via ADMIN_EMAILS); partly supersedes DEC-01 and the admin part of DEC-09.
decisions.reason: The app is for a small hand-picked group, so public signup (code review finding CR-01) was the top risk: anyone could spend the shared Claude subscription and make the owner's Gmail relay email third parties. Proving mailbox ownership with an emailed link doubles as email verification and as the missing password reset (GAP-04). Rejected: invite codes or an allowlist with open signup (people could still create accounts before being vetted) and an admin approval queue (more UI for no gain).

known_gaps.summary: PDF parsing has not been exercised with a real PDF; tests only cover TXT and DOCX uploads.
known_gaps.note: H4 added tests that parse a real (hand-built) PDF, a page cap and a corrupt PDF. Still worth trying once with a real-world multi-page resume PDF; tracked in H6.

known_gaps.summary: Every user shares the owner's Claude subscription usage limits.
known_gaps.note: Calls are budgeted per user (25/day by default) and concurrency-capped.

known_gaps.summary: python-jobspy scraping of LinkedIn/Indeed violates those sites' terms and is fragile (rate limits, blocks); it must stay opt-in and isolated. results_per_query applies per site (3 -> up to 6 jobs).
known_gaps.note: The old claim that ingestion is not scheduled is obsolete: the worker schedules it since milestone 7.

known_gaps.summary: No email verification or password reset. Any admin can replace the shared Claude token, and the question/unsubscribe links rely on signed tokens only, so account and admin passwords must be strong.
known_gaps.note: Addressed by backlog item H1. Planned fix: REQ-18 / DESIGN-01. The emailed set-password link proves mailbox ownership, so it doubles as email verification and as the missing password reset.

known_gaps.summary: Postfix direct-delivery mode needs SPF/DKIM/DMARC records and a host that allows outbound port 25; relay mode (Gmail) is the safe default.
Follow-up questions may re-ask for status fields left as 'Not sure' in the questionnaire (e.g. visa sponsorship).
Documents/links data from before the file store was not migrated (only test data existed); the unused docker volume jobfinder_uploads can be removed.

Dev-only quirks: running the worker on the host (for the logged-in claude CLI) needs STORE_DIR pointing at the same files as the api because the docker volume is not visible from the host; the first SMTP connection from a host process to the Mailpit container can take several seconds on macOS.
Seniority is inferred from the job title only and is coarse (e.g. 'Account Manager' is labelled manager).
known_gaps.note: The LLM scoring is the real judgement.

known_gaps.summary: Salary is known for roughly half of the cached jobs (structured fields or parsed from the description); unknown pay never excludes a job.
The same posting repeated on one board (different requisitions) is cached as separate rows (~90 same-title groups).
known_gaps.note: Matching collapses to one row per dedupe_hash since milestone 5; the cache keeps the duplicates, which is harmless.

known_gaps.summary: companies.yaml covers 27 companies only; add rows to widen coverage (slugs must be verified against the live board APIs).

A successful AI call from the Docker worker with a REAL token has not been seen yet (only the failure path with a fake token). The owner must paste a real `claude setup-token` token on the AI setup page and run Test connection.
known_gaps.note: Needs the owner; tracked in backlog item H6.

known_gaps.summary: The shared token can expire or be revoked; the AI setup page then shows 'Last call failed (auth)' and the wizard shows the connect notice.
Scoring is slow and limited: about 25 seconds per job with the CLI, so the default 25 jobs/day is roughly an 11-minute background run; the rest wait ('N more promising jobs are waiting').
known_gaps.note: Raise MATCH_DAILY_LLM_BUDGET / AI_MAX_CONCURRENCY only if the subscription allows.

known_gaps.summary: Location matching is heuristic (substring/alias based, e.g. NYC, SF, US states); odd location strings can be missed or over-matched, and remote roles restricted to other countries still reach the LLM.
Some postings in the cache are months old and still active on the company's board; the feed shows 'Posted X months ago' and the prefilter down-weights stale ones.
Frontend has no automated tests beyond one-off Playwright runs.
known_gaps.note: 27 Vitest + Testing Library tests: sign-in, set/reset password, matches feed (Apply links), emailed questions link, routing/admin nav, safeHttpUrl. Run with `cd frontend && npm test`.

known_gaps.summary: Generated letters can still lightly embellish (e.g. 'I also enjoy building across the stack', linking two true facts that the profile doesn't link). There is no automatic fact-check pass.
known_gaps.note: Mitigated by prompt rules that forbid invented facts, absences and feelings, and an on-page warning to read the letter before sending.

known_gaps.summary: Letters are plain text/Word without a contact header or date (the profile has no phone/address); the user adds those when sending.
Email delivery to the inbox (not spam) is unverified: Gmail accepted a test message from the relay, but only the owner can confirm where it landed.
known_gaps.note: Needs the owner; tracked in backlog item H6. (H3 changed delivery to at-most-once per day: the digest is claimed before SMTP and released if SMTP fails.)

known_gaps.summary: The scheduler and daily emails are live in the Docker stack: real users whose chosen hour arrives receive real email through the owner's Gmail relay (Gmail's ~500/day limit applies) and ingestion/matching consume the shared Claude subscription.
known_gaps.note: SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false or the per-user Settings toggles turn this off. Once REQ-18 ships, only emails the owner has added can receive any of this.

known_gaps.summary: Question emails are sent once; there are no reminder emails for unanswered questions (they stay in the in-app inbox).
Users created before timezone capture have timezone UTC until they change it in Settings.
Profiles extracted before the `name` field have no name (cover letters end with just 'Sincerely,').
known_gaps.note: Mitigated: the Profile > Background page can now set the name.

known_gaps.summary: Once DESIGN-01 is built, signing in for the first time (and resetting a password) depends on outbound email working: if the SMTP relay fails, nobody can set or reset a password. A mistyped invitee email also means the person never receives the link.
known_gaps.note: Mitigated by the planned owner break-glass CLI (reset-link prints a one-time link instead of emailing it) and by the existing SQL route for adding users. Tracked in backlog item H1.

code_review.scope: Whole repository as it stands. The project is not a git repository, so there was no diff to review.
code_review.method: The /code-review skill could not review anything (no git history to diff, and it treated an extra argument as part of the path). Three parallel reviewer agents and then shell commands were blocked by the auto-mode safety check. The review was therefore done directly by reading the highest-risk files and tracing each suspected defect through the code; every finding marked 'read in this review' was confirmed against the code.
limitations: Targeted, not exhaustive: only the files listed in files_read were re-read in this review.
No dynamic testing, dependency audit or penetration testing was done.
Findings marked 'from authorship, not re-read' rest on knowledge of code written earlier in the project and should be re-checked when fixed.
code_review.recommendation: Put the project under git with a committed baseline and run /code-review again so it reviews a real diff; re-verify each finding when fixing it.

findings.summary: Self-signup is open to anyone who can reach the app: there is no invite, allowlist or email verification.
findings.failure_scenario: An outsider signs up with victim@example.com and finishes a minimal profile; the daily email and questions are then sent to the victim through the owner's Gmail relay. Many accounts each trigger matching (up to 25 LLM calls per day each) on the shared Claude subscription.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove self-signup: invite-only accounts activated by an emailed set-password link, per DESIGN-01 (REQ-18).

findings.summary: SECRET_KEY defaults to the public string 'dev-insecure-change-me' and backend/.env does not set it, so the running stack signs tokens with a publicly known key.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone who has read the source can forge a question-link or unsubscribe token for any user id: read that user's open questions and job titles, answer or skip them, or unsubscribe them. Once DESIGN-01 adds emailed password-reset links signed with the same key, the same forgery would also let them reset any account's password: full account takeover.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse to start with the default key outside dev (or generate and persist a random one) and set it in backend/.env. This must ship together with DESIGN-01, not after it.

findings.summary: argon2 hashing and verification run synchronously inside async handlers, and nothing in the API is rate-limited.
findings.failure_scenario: A flood of login or signup requests blocks the event loop for tens of milliseconds each, stalling every other request; passwords can be brute-forced without throttling and the preview-email endpoint can be called without limit.
findings.suggested_fix: Run hashing in a threadpool and add per-IP/per-email rate limits (app or nginx limit_req). DESIGN-01 requires this for login and the password-reset endpoints, and needs nginx's forwarded client IP to be trusted so per-IP limits are meaningful.

findings.summary: Account enumeration: signup answers 409 'Email already registered', and login for an unknown email skips password hashing so it returns noticeably faster.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker probes a list of addresses and learns which have accounts, by message or by response time.
findings.suggested_fix: Planned in DESIGN-01: signup (and its 409) is removed; login and link requests return identical generic responses and verify against a dummy hash for unknown or pending emails.

findings.summary: The SSRF guard resolves DNS and then httpx resolves again (rebinding window), and the response body is not size-capped before resp.text and synchronous text extraction.
findings.failure_scenario: A user submits a URL whose DNS answers a public address for the check and an internal one for the fetch, or points at a huge or slow-drip response: the API fetches an internal address or exhausts memory and blocks the event loop.
findings.suggested_fix: Stream with a byte cap and a total deadline, connect to the validated IP, and run extraction in a thread.

findings.summary: Uploaded files are parsed synchronously inside the async handler with no page limit beyond the 10 MB cap.
findings.failure_scenario: A large or crafted PDF keeps pdfplumber busy for seconds and the whole API stops answering other requests.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse in a threadpool with a page cap and a timeout.

findings.summary: A task whose handler leaves the DB session in a failed state makes queue.fail raise inside run_task; the exception is never retrieved, the task stays 'running', and reap_stuck requeues it every 15 minutes with no attempt cap. run_task also crashes if the task row is missing.
findings.failure_scenario: A poison task (for example one hitting a DB error) is re-run forever, repeating its LLM calls, while the worker logs nothing useful.
findings.suggested_fix: Roll back before queue.fail, add a done-callback that logs task-future exceptions, and mark tasks failed in reap_stuck once attempts reach the cap.

findings.summary: STUCK_AFTER is 15 minutes but nothing refreshes locked_at while a task runs, and the reaper only runs every 300 loop iterations.
findings.failure_scenario: A long task (a bigger match budget, or the sequential daily-email tick doing LLM and SMTP per user) is requeued while still running and executed twice: double LLM spend and a duplicate daily email.
findings.suggested_fix: Heartbeat locked_at while running, or use per-kind timeouts, and reap on a fixed schedule.

findings.summary: enqueue(dedupe=True) is a check-then-insert with no unique constraint, so it is not atomic.
findings.failure_scenario: A double-click on 'Find new matches' (or an API request racing the scheduler) inserts two tasks and runs two matching passes for the same user at once, doubling LLM spend.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a partial unique index on (kind, user_id, payload) for queued/running tasks, or take an advisory lock.

findings.summary: find_candidates loads every active job with its full description (about 7,000 rows of up to 20 KB) per user per run and does CPU-bound filtering inside the async worker.
findings.failure_scenario: With several users, each matching run spikes memory by tens to hundreds of MB and blocks the worker's event loop for seconds, delaying other tasks and heartbeats; cost grows with users times jobs.
findings.suggested_fix: Select only the needed columns, push more filtering into SQL, and run the CPU-bound scoring off the event loop.

findings.summary: job.url (from ATS or JobSpy data) is rendered as an href with no scheme check and is not validated at ingestion; the same pattern is used in Matches.tsx and the email's Apply link (those two not re-read).
findings.failure_scenario: A scraped posting with a javascript: URL runs script in the app's origin when a user clicks Apply.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept only http(s) URLs at ingestion and when rendering in the UI and the email.
findings.verified: MatchDetail.tsx read in this review; Matches.tsx and the email template from authorship, not re-read

findings.summary: The daily email is at-least-once: the message is sent over SMTP first and the matches/questions are marked sent afterwards.
findings.failure_scenario: A crash or DB error between the send and the commit (or a duplicate run from CR-08) makes the next hourly tick send the same email again.
findings.suggested_fix: Record a 'sending' state before the SMTP call or otherwise make the send idempotent, or accept and document at-least-once delivery.

findings.summary: The unsubscribe link changes state on GET.
findings.failure_scenario: Email security scanners and link previewers fetch the URL and silently unsubscribe users who never clicked it (RFC 8058 reserves state changes for the POST one-click).
findings.suggested_fix: Make GET show a confirmation page with a POST button; only POST unsubscribes.

findings.summary: nginx sets no security headers: no CSP, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options or Referrer-Policy.
findings.failure_scenario: The settings and AI-setup pages can be framed by another site (clickjacking), and nothing limits the impact of an injected script.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the standard security headers in nginx.

findings.summary: Session tokens are stored in plaintext in the database and expired sessions are never pruned.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone who can read the sessions table can use live tokens as-is, and the table grows without bound.
findings.suggested_fix: Store a hash of the token and prune expired rows on login or on a schedule.

findings.summary: On timeout the Claude process group is killed with SIGKILL but proc.wait() is never awaited.
findings.failure_scenario: Each timed-out call leaves a zombie process until the event loop reaps it, so repeated timeouts accumulate defunct processes in the worker container.
findings.suggested_fix: await proc.wait() after killing the process group (and on cancellation).

findings.summary: Several important behaviours have no tests: the worker main loop and reaper, the run_task failure path with a DB error, concurrent enqueue dedupe, fetch_page_text redirect/size handling, real PDF parsing, and the whole frontend.
findings.failure_scenario: Regressions in the queue, worker and fetch paths (where CR-05, CR-07, CR-08 and CR-09 live) would go unnoticed by the test suite.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the missing backend tests and automated frontend tests for the core flows.
findings.resolution_note: Added tests for run_task failures, heartbeat, reaper, concurrent dedupe, fetch_page_text (IP pinning, redirects, size, deadline), real/corrupt/page-capped PDFs, and frontend tests (27). Not covered: the worker's main() polling loop as a whole (its parts are tested).

findings.summary: The plain-text daily email was HTML-escaped (select_autoescape matched .j2), so & became & and apply URLs with several query parameters were corrupted.
findings.suggested_fix: Escape only html.j2 and not txt.j2; text and HTML parts tested separately.
findings.verified: found by /code-review of baseline commit 59a1be8; CR-18 reproduced by rendering the template

findings.summary: The two-parse cap was released on timeout while the thread kept running, so repeated slow uploads could pile up threads and occupy the default executor used for DNS lookups.
findings.suggested_fix: Dedicated 2-thread pool and a slot released only when the parse really finishes; a full parser answers 503.
findings.verified: found by /code-review of baseline commit 59a1be8; CR-18 reproduced by rendering the template

findings.summary: The 6-hour catch-up window did not cross local midnight, so an evening digest missed at its hour was never sent (digest_hour 19 or later).
findings.suggested_fix: is_due now compares against the most recent scheduled instant, which may be yesterday's.
findings.verified: found by /code-review of baseline commit 59a1be8; CR-18 reproduced by rendering the template

findings.summary: In development React StrictMode ran the effect twice; the first run cleared the URL fragment so the second found no token.
findings.suggested_fix: Token read once in a useState initializer; the effect only clears the address bar.
findings.verified: found by /code-review of baseline commit 59a1be8; CR-18 reproduced by rendering the template

planned_designs.title: Invite-only access with an emailed set/reset password link
goals: Only people the owner has added can ever get an account or receive email from the system
No separate password-reset feature to build: first-time password setup and forgotten-password use the same emailed link
Give a pending person a clear way in without revealing to outsiders which emails exist
non_goals: An admin screen for adding users (the owner inserts rows manually)

users: Make these columns nullable and drop their DB defaults so that INSERT INTO users (email) VALUES ('x@y.com') works with everything else NULL: password_hash, timezone, digest_hour, digest_enabled, question_emails_enabled, is_admin
Add activated_at timestamptz NULL; created_at keeps its default
Store emails lowercase and add CHECK (email = lower(email)) so manual inserts cannot create look-alike duplicates
pending = password_hash IS NULL; active = password_hash IS NOT NULL
data_model.rate_events: New table rate_events(id, kind, key, created_at) with index (kind, key, created_at); the worker prunes old rows. Used for login-failure and link-request limits.
migration: Relax the NOT NULL constraints and drop the server defaults listed above
Backfill activated_at = created_at for existing users (they already have passwords)
Existing accounts, passwords, sessions and profiles are untouched
activation_populates: an empty profiles row (status {}, background {}, version 1)

flows.name: Sign-in page (/login)
steps: Fields: email and password, a Sign in button, and an always-visible link 'First time here, or forgot your password? Email me a link'
There is no sign-up toggle

flows.name: POST /api/auth/login
steps: Unknown email, pending account and wrong password all return the same 401 'Invalid email or password'
When there is no password hash to check, verify against a dummy argon2 hash so response time does not reveal the difference
Hash verification runs in a threadpool; throttled by the rate limits below

flows.name: POST /api/auth/password-reset/request {email}
steps: Always answers 202 with the same text: 'If that address has access, we've emailed a link. It expires in 60 minutes.'
Only an existing row (pending or active) that is not rate limited gets an email, sent in the background so response time does not leak existence
Subject is 'Set your JobFinder password' for pending accounts and 'Reset your JobFinder password' for active ones
Unknown emails receive nothing, so the endpoint cannot be used to email strangers

flows.name: The emailed link
steps: {PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/reset-password#token=...  The token is in the URL fragment so it never reaches server logs or the Referer header
Signed with its own salt/purpose ('password-reset') so a question-link or unsubscribe token cannot be replayed here
Contains a fingerprint of the current password hash (empty for pending accounts), so the link stops working as soon as the password is set or changed: single use
Expires after PASSWORD_LINK_TTL_MINUTES (default 60)

flows.name: POST /api/auth/password-reset/confirm {token, password, timezone}
steps: Validate signature, purpose, age and the password fingerprint; any failure returns one generic 400 with a pointer to request a new link
Password rules: 10 to 256 characters and not equal to the email
In one transaction: hash the password in a threadpool and set password_hash; if the user was pending, populate the fields listed under activation_populates and create the profile row
Delete all existing sessions for the user, create a fresh session and set the cookie: the user is signed in and lands in onboarding

flows.name: Owner break-glass (planned CLI, SQL also works)
steps: python -m jobfinder.cli add-user --email x@y.com  (inserts the email-only row)
python -m jobfinder.cli reset-link --email x@y.com  (prints a one-time link instead of emailing it, for when SMTP is down)
python -m jobfinder.cli list-users

removed: The sign-up form, the Sign up / Log in toggle and AuthProvider.signup in the frontend
The first-account-is-admin rule (admin only via ADMIN_EMAILS)
Signup tests and the signup-time timezone capture (timezone moves to the set-password step)
active_only_touchpoints: notify/daily.py: due_users and is_due must skip rows with NULL digest_hour / not active
api/settings.py and the UserOut model: nullable-safe
matching enqueue (enqueue_for_active_users): pending users have no profile row, so they are naturally skipped
scheduling/handlers.py daily_emails and collect_questions: only active users
auth/security.py current_user: only active users can hold sessions
config: Login and link-request rate limit settings
ADMIN_EMAILS becomes the only way to be admin
Configure uvicorn to trust nginx's forwarded headers (--forwarded-allow-ips) so per-IP limits see the real client address instead of nginx's

rate_limits.link_requests: 3 per hour per email with a 60 second cooldown, and 10 per hour per IP
rate_limits.failed_logins: 10 per 15 minutes per email and 30 per 15 minutes per IP, then HTTP 429

security_notes: CR-01 (open signup) is removed by design: only emails the owner adds can ever receive mail
CR-04 (enumeration): generic login error, identical link-request response, equalised timing
CR-03: hashing off the event loop and the rate limits above are required parts of this work

CR-02 becomes more serious: reset links are signed with SECRET_KEY, so a forged token would be full account takeover. The startup guard that refuses the default key must ship together with this feature, not after it
CR-14: send Referrer-Policy: no-referrer on the reset page; CR-15 (hashed session tokens) is a natural companion change
Inherent risk: whoever controls a user's mailbox can take over the account (true of any email-based reset)

choices_made.choice: Message for a pending account that tries to sign in
choices_made.chosen: Same generic error as any failed login, with the 'email me a link' option always visible on the page
choices_made.alternative: Tell the person explicitly that no password is set yet (friendlier, but reveals which invited emails are not activated)

choices_made.chosen: URL fragment (#token=), read by the page and posted to the API
choices_made.alternative: Query string or path (simpler, but ends up in logs and Referer headers)

choices_made.chosen: 60 minutes, configurable; people can request a new link at any time
choices_made.alternative: 24 hours for first-time setup (more convenient, larger exposure window)

risks: Sign-in now depends on outbound email: if the SMTP relay fails nobody can set or reset a password (mitigated by the break-glass CLI; tracked as GAP-26)
Many code paths assume non-null user columns; each must be reviewed for NULL safety (see active_only_touchpoints)
A typo in an email the owner types means the invitee never gets the link
tests: Unknown, pending and wrong-password logins return identical responses and comparable timing
Link request for an unknown vs a known email returns identical responses; only the known one sends mail
Token: single use, expiry, tampering and wrong-purpose rejection, and invalidation after the password changes
Confirm populates a pending row, creates the profile, signs the user in and removes their other sessions
Pending users receive no digest, no questions and no matching
Rate limiting for logins and link requests, using the real client IP behind nginx
NULL-safe code paths for pending rows
Playwright run: owner inserts an email row -> person requests a link -> opens it -> sets a password -> is signed in -> completes onboarding
